solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rude track on the radio (6)

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a course is a track, as for racing

annotation.surface: A complaint about an offensive song played on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Track' pulls towards a song, which suits the radio; here it is a racecourse.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coarse jokes and rude jokes are the same vulgar thing.

clue.text: Take heart from sloppy act of affection (6)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and taking it away removes those letters

annotation.surface: A half-hearted, slapdash show of love that one might find encouraging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take heart' reads as 'be encouraged'; it is an instruction to cut out the middle of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun names a gentle stroke given out of fondness, so a descriptive phrase for it.

clue.text: Seeming enticing to change sides (9)

indicators.note: L (left) swaps for R (right), one side for the other

annotation.surface: A politician whose attraction lies in being ready to defect.
annotation.walkthrough: L and R are the standard abbreviations for left and right, so 'change sides' swaps one for the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'appearing tired' and 'seeming tired' mean the same.

clue.text: Rose starts to trail over turf borders (5)

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters
the turf forms a border on either side of the letters

blocks.note: first letters of trail and over

annotation.surface: A gardening note: a rose trailing over the edges of a lawn.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Rose' a flower; it is the past tense of rise.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense of rise to one's feet, as in 'he rose from his chair'.

clue.text: Take away work from Kandinsky? (8)

blocks.note: the formal verb for remove or extract
Wassily Kandinsky pioneered non-figurative painting; the question mark flags an example

annotation.surface: Someone lifting a painting from a Kandinsky exhibition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take away' sounds like carrying a picture off; it is the formal verb.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to remove; the other, by example, is a non-figurative painting such as Kandinsky made.

clue.text: Space that man’s taken in airship above a secure stately home (8,6)

indicators.note: the airship takes the other letters inside itself
in a down answer, what is above comes first

blocks.note: a blimp is a small airship
an en is a printer's space
to lace is to fasten or secure

annotation.surface: An airship carrying a man and some space, flying over a guarded country house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Space' is the printer's en, not room. The answer is the Churchill family seat in Oxfordshire.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is one of England's grandest country houses, birthplace of Churchill.

clue.text: On railway, stray within dictator’s land (9)

indicators.note: the stray goes inside the dictator
in a down answer, one part sits on top of the other

annotation.surface: Someone wandering along the railway into a tyrant's country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On railway' opens the clue but its letters come last: in a down answer, the rest sits on top of the railway.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ruler's territory is the land under his control.

clue.text: Walk better when unclothed (5)

indicators.note: a word stripped of its clothes loses its outside letters

blocks.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

annotation.surface: The advice that walking goes better naked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like 'improved'; it is 'one who bets'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, specifically a slow, leisurely walk.

clue.text: Metal fastener mounted on top of Gatling gun (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting something makes it read upwards
the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue

blocks.note: a nut fastens a bolt; mounted, it reads upwards
the Sten was a British submachine gun

annotation.surface: A bolt fixed to the top of a Gatling gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gatling gun' reads as one weapon but splits: its first letter, then a different gun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a hard, dense metallic element used in filaments.

clue.text: Ensuring continued service from group if fortune fails (6-8)

indicators.note: when the letters fail they fall apart and reform

annotation.surface: A band planning how to keep playing if their luck runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fails' looks like part of the band's bad-luck story; it is what breaks the letters up.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: the term means designing something so it keeps working as times change.

clue.text: Have young professional cut sandwiches (9)

indicators.note: the cut holds the professional between its parts, like bread round a filling

annotation.surface: A young professional reducing a sandwich order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Young professional' is a set phrase, but 'young' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: animals that breed produce offspring, their young.

clue.text: Masked sidekick to plunder home (5)

annotation.surface: A masked accomplice about to burgle a house.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a burglar's mate; the definition is a comic-book one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Batman's young partner wears a domino mask.

clue.text: Small old man heated bath (3)

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father, pa

annotation.surface: A little old man who has been warmed up in the bath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heated' looks like it describes the old man; it belongs with 'bath'.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means a warm mineral bath or hot tub, as well as the resort built round one.

clue.text: Money book heroine swipes in valour (11)

indicators.note: the heroine grabs IN and holds it

blocks.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's heroine

annotation.surface: A storybook heroine bravely snatching cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In valour' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is letters to be swiped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doughty is an old word for brave, and this is its noun.

clue.text: Intermediate male violinist wanting tips (6)

indicators.note: the violinist lacks the letters at either end

annotation.surface: A so-so male violinist hoping for gratuities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like money for the busker; it means ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: the middle stage is the intermediate one.

clue.text: Set off from old housing somewhere in Berkshire (9)

indicators.note: the old word houses the place

blocks.note: Eton is a town in Berkshire, home of the school

annotation.surface: Someone setting out from an old house in Berkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' suggests departing; here it is setting off a bomb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the explosives sense: a charge that was set off went bang.

clue.text: Love oldies broadcast after one (7)

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters the letters
the anagram comes after the one

annotation.surface: Someone who loves hearing golden oldies on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture; it scatters the letters of 'oldies'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, pitched stronger: to love to the point of worship.

clue.text: They feign patriotism deposing leader in revolution (9)

indicators.note: the first letter is thrown out
the letters are turned over into a new order

blocks.note: PATRIOTISM without its first letter P

annotation.surface: Rebels faking loyalty to their country while overthrowing its ruler.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all politics; 'deposing leader' and 'revolution' are instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: people who mimic others pretend to be what they are not.

clue.text: Nearby upside-down pudding is sealed (6,2)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the word turned upside down reads upwards

blocks.note: pud = pudding; upside-down, it reads upwards

annotation.surface: A pineapple upside-down pudding next door, cling-filmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down pudding' is a real dessert, but 'upside-down' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jar closed up tight has been sealed.

clue.text: One leaving property on a hill (7)

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a tor is a rocky hill

annotation.surface: Someone moving out of a house on a hillside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaving property' sounds like moving house; it means bequeathing it.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal term: the maker of a legacy, one who leaves property by will.

clue.text: Therapist from outskirts of Portsmouth regularly seen by a sailor (6)

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters
take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: first and last letters of Portsmouth
every second letter of 'by a sailor'

annotation.surface: A therapist from the edge of a naval town, visited by a seaman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seen' only joins; the regular letters come from 'by a sailor', not from 'seen'.
annotation.definitionFit: The British short form for a physiotherapist, a therapist for muscles and joints.

clue.text: Sort to ignore if posh (6)

indicators.note: ignoring IF leaves it out of the word

blocks.note: if as itself; ignored, so removed

annotation.surface: A snob's rule: the kind of person to shun if they are posh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a noun, 'kind'; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: both mean stylish and upmarket.

clue.text: Japanese food beginning to sell loads around Scottish town (4,7)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
S plus OODLES goes around the town

blocks.note: Oban is a port on the west coast of Scotland

annotation.surface: A Japanese restaurant starting to do big business in a Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' applies to the S and the loads together: the town sits between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: buckwheat noodles are a staple Japanese dish.

clue.text: Former PM vacated beautiful carriage (5)

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: carriage = bearing or manner, as does air

annotation.surface: An ex-prime minister stepping out of a fine coach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle; it means the way one holds oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Tony Blair was UK prime minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Brief scrap with small beast (5)

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A short fight with a little animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight; it is a shred.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tiny mouse-like insectivore.

clue.text: Trouble from ChatGPT, say, source of lies (3)

indicators.note: a word's source is its first letter

blocks.note: ChatGPT is an example of AI

annotation.surface: Complaining that a chatbot makes things up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' reads as a noun in the surface; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: what ails you troubles you.

clue.text: Resistance to be in silly sketch (5)

indicators.note: R is placed inside the other word

annotation.surface: Refusing to appear in a foolish comedy sketch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' reads as a comedy skit; it is a rough drawing or plan.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a preliminary version of a drawing or document.

clue.text: Get notes from debtors having low level of interest (9)

blocks.note: to incur is to get, as a charge
an IOU is a note of debt

annotation.surface: A lender earning little interest on debtors' promissory notes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interest' is financial in the surface; in the definition it is curiosity.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: lacking curiosity, taking little interest.

clue.text: Soldier and third of regiment enthralled by dusky model (8)

indicators.note: the third letter of the word
held captive inside the other word

annotation.surface: A soldier and a regiment captivated by a dark-skinned model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' sounds like a person; it is an example or pattern.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pattern or standard example to follow.

clue.text: Idiot Yankee obstructed by second being devious (6)

indicators.note: the S gets in the way, stuck between the letters

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A fool of an American held up for a moment while being sneaky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' looks like an American; it is just the letter Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: a twisty mind, like a devious one, never goes straight.
